title: Quiet Time and Thank-You Time
bigQuestion: What are some ways people are quiet or say thank you?

story.title: One Minute of Quiet
story.kicker: The teacher rings a soft bell, and the room gets still.
paragraphs: Ms. Ruiz rings a soft bell. "Now we have one minute of quiet," she says. "You may use it any way that helps you feel calm."
Ben closes his eyes. He breathes in slowly and out slowly. Grace folds her hands. She says a silent prayer. Ali looks out the window at a tree.
Rosa hums a song in her head. Dev just sits still and rests. Nobody talks. Nobody laughs at anyone. Everyone lets the others be.
The bell rings again. "How do you feel?" asks Ms. Ruiz. "Calm," says Ben. "Ready," says Dev. Each child used the quiet in their own way.
story.think: What did each child do with the quiet minute? What helps you feel calm?

lessons.title: Thanks Before a Meal
lessons.mainIdea: Many families say thank you before or after they eat.
reading: Look at a family at dinner. Before they eat, some Christian families hold hands. They say a short prayer called *grace*. It thanks God for the food.
Jewish families say blessings over bread and after meals. Muslims often say bismillah, in the name of God, before eating. Some families just say thanks to the cook.

words.d: a short prayer of thanks said before or after a meal

look.title: Words from the Torah
look.text: When thou hast eaten and art full, then thou shalt bless the LORD thy God for the good land which he hath given thee.
look.prompt: When does this verse say to give thanks?

choices: A short prayer of thanks at a meal
check.why: Grace is a prayer of thanks said at a meal.

check.q: Who often says bismillah before eating?
check.why: Many Muslims say bismillah, in the name of God, before eating.

check.q: Deuteronomy 8:10 says to give thanks when?
check.why: The verse says to bless God after eating and being full.

lessons.title: Candles on Friday Night
lessons.mainIdea: Many Jewish families light candles and say a blessing to start Shabbat.
reading: It is Friday. The sun is going down. In many Jewish homes, someone lights two candles. They say a *blessing*, words that thank God.
This starts *Shabbat*, the day of rest. It lasts until Saturday night. Families eat, sing, and rest together.

words.d: words that thank God or ask for good
the Jewish day of rest, from Friday evening to Saturday evening

look.title: A Week and Its Rest Day
look.cite: The Jewish calendar week; see Exodus 20:8-11
look.prompt: How many days come before Shabbat?

check.why: Shabbat starts at sundown on Friday.

check.q: What do many families light to start Shabbat?
check.why: Many Jewish families light two candles.
Shabbat is the Jewish day of rest.

lessons.title: Five Prayers a Day
lessons.mainIdea: Many Muslims pray five times each day, facing toward Mecca.
reading: Look at the small rug on the floor. A Muslim man stands on it. He bows. Then he kneels and touches his forehead to the rug.
This prayer is called *salat*. Muslims pray it five times a day. They face toward Mecca, a holy city. A rug keeps the place clean.

words.d: the prayer Muslims say five times a day
a holy city in Saudi Arabia that Muslims face when they pray

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Dawn. Noon. Afternoon. Sunset. Night. Five times the prayer rug comes out. Five times it is rolled up again.
look.prompt: Count the times. Why might a rug help at each one?

check.q: How many times a day do many Muslims pray salat?
check.why: Salat is prayed five times each day.

check.q: Which way do Muslims face to pray?

lessons.title: A Song of Praise
lessons.mainIdea: Many people sing to give thanks and to pray.
reading: Listen. In a church, people sing hymns. A *hymn* is a song of praise to God. In a Hindu temple, people sing as a lamp is waved.
At a gurdwara, Sikhs sing words from their holy book. Songs help many people feel close to God and to each other.

words.d: a song of praise, often sung in church

look.title: A Song from the Psalms
look.text: O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
look.prompt: What does this song ask people to do?

check.why: A hymn is a song of praise.

check.q: Where do Sikhs sing words from their holy book?
Psalm 136:1 asks people to do what?
check.why: The psalm says, give thanks unto the Lord.

lessons.title: Sitting and Breathing
lessons.mainIdea: Many Buddhists sit still and pay attention to their breath.
reading: Look at a woman sitting on a cushion. Her back is tall. Her eyes are soft. She feels her breath go in and out.
This is *meditation*. Many Buddhists meditate to calm the mind. Many other people sit and breathe quietly too.

words.d: sitting still and paying calm attention, like to your breath

look.title: Try It
look.text: Sit tall. Put one hand on your tummy. Breathe in slowly. Feel your hand rise. Breathe out slowly. Feel it fall. Do this three times.
look.prompt: How did your body feel after three slow breaths?

check.why: Meditation means sitting still and paying calm attention.

check.q: Who often meditates to calm the mind?
check.why: Meditation is a key Buddhist practice.

check.q: What does the woman pay attention to?
check.why: She feels her breath go in and out.

lessons.title: Being Kind When Others Are Quiet
lessons.mainIdea: We stay calm and kind when someone else is praying or being quiet.
reading: Some families pray. Some sit in silence. Some do none of these things. Every family is *welcome* to its own way.
When someone is quiet or praying, we can help. We use soft voices. We wait. We do not laugh. This is being *respectful*.

words.d: treating people and their ways with care
glad to be included, just as you are

look.title: What Would You Do?
look.text: Your friend's grandpa is praying on his rug. You want to ask him a question. Your friend puts a finger to her lips.
look.prompt: What could you do while you wait?

check.q: Your friend is praying. What is respectful?

check.why: Some families pray and some do not; all are welcome.

choices: Treating people and their ways with care
check.why: Being respectful means treating others with care.

review.why: Shabbat is the Jewish day of rest.

review.q: Who prays salat five times a day?
A prayer of thanks at a meal is called what?
Sitting still and watching your breath is called what?

review.why: A hymn is a song of praise.

review.q: Someone near you is praying. What can you do?
choices: Use a soft voice and wait
review.why: Being quiet and waiting is respectful.
